def: An employment contract with no end date, which continues until one of the parties terminates it.

formal.ex: The Employee is engaged under an [[indefinite-term employment contract]] governed by French law.

everyday.ex: After two fixed-term contracts, they finally offered her a [[permanent contract]].
everyday.ex_us: After two fixed-term contracts, they finally offered her a [[permanent position]].

collocations: to be on a permanent contract
to offer someone a permanent contract
to move onto a permanent contract
note_fr: Ne dites pas « undetermined contract » ni « unlimited contract ». Aux États-Unis, « permanent » ne garantit rien : l'emploi reste en principe « at-will » ; on y parle plutôt de « regular full-time employee ».

explain.written: The CDI (contrat à durée indéterminée) is the standard French employment contract: it has no end date and can only be terminated on the grounds and by the procedures laid down by law.
explain.spoken: A CDI is basically a permanent contract - there's no end date, and the employer can't end it without a valid reason.

def: An employment contract that ends on a set date or when a specific task or event is completed.

formal.ex: A [[fixed-term employment contract]] may not be used to fill a post linked to the company's normal and permanent activity.

everyday.ex: She's on a six-month [[fixed-term contract]] covering someone's maternity leave.
everyday.ex_us: She's on a six-month [[temporary contract]] covering someone's maternity leave.

collocations: to be on a fixed-term contract
to take someone on on a fixed-term basis
note_fr: Pas de « determined contract » ni de « limited contract ». Au Royaume-Uni et aux États-Unis, le recours au contrat à durée déterminée n'est pas limité à une liste de motifs comme en France : expliquez-le toujours.

explain.written: The CDD (contrat à durée déterminée) is a fixed-term contract which, under French law, may only be used for specific temporary needs such as replacing an absent employee or covering a temporary increase in activity.
explain.spoken: A CDD is a fixed-term contract, but in France you can only use one for a genuinely temporary need - covering an absence, say, or a seasonal peak.

def: Working the standard number of hours for the job, as opposed to reduced hours.

formal.ex: The Employee shall be employed [[on a full-time basis]].

everyday.ex: Is the role [[full-time]], or would you consider four days a week?

note_fr: « Full-time » s'emploie comme adjectif et comme adverbe (« she works full-time »), sans « at » : jamais « at full time ». L'ETP se dit « full-time equivalent » ou « FTE ».

def: Working fewer hours than a full-time employee in the same organisation.

formal.ex: The Employee is engaged [[on a part-time basis]] for twenty-four hours per week.

everyday.ex: He's asked [[to go part-time]] when he comes back from parental leave.

collocations: to cut down to three days a week
note_fr: Évitez le calque « partial time ». Un salarié à temps partiel est « a part-timer » ou « a part-time employee ». Le « 80 % » français se dit plutôt en jours : « she works four days a week ».

def: Work done for a client company by someone who is employed and paid by an employment agency.

formal.ex: The company may have recourse to [[temporary agency work]] only for a precise and temporary task.
formal.ex_us: The company may have recourse to [[temporary staffing]] only for a precise and temporary task.

everyday.ex: We've had to bring in [[agency staff]] to get through the Christmas rush.
everyday.ex_us: We've had to bring in [[temps]] to get through the Christmas rush.

informal.ex: She did a year of [[temping]] before she landed a proper job.

note_fr: « Interim » est un faux ami : « an interim manager » est un manager de transition, « in the interim » signifie « entre-temps ». L'intérimaire est « an agency worker » (UK) ou « a temp » (surtout US) ; l'entreprise de travail temporaire, « a staffing agency » (US) ou « an employment agency » (UK).

def: A contract combining paid work with structured training that leads to a recognised qualification.

formal.ex: The [[apprenticeship agreement]] shall specify the qualification for which the apprentice is being trained.

everyday.ex: He's doing an [[apprenticeship]] with us while he finishes his master's.

note_fr: « Alternance » n'a pas d'équivalent exact : dites « a work-study programme » (US « program ») ou « an apprenticeship ». Ne confondez pas « apprentice » (apprenti), « trainee » (stagiaire en formation interne) et « intern » (stagiaire étudiant).

def: A UK arrangement under which the employer does not guarantee any minimum number of working hours.

formal.ex: Under a [[zero-hours contract]], the employer is under no obligation to offer any work.
formal.ex_us: Under an [[on-call employment arrangement]], the employer is under no obligation to offer any work.

everyday.ex: Most of the bar staff are on [[zero-hours contracts]], so their pay varies a lot from week to week.
everyday.ex_us: Most of the bar staff do [[on-call work]], so their pay varies a lot from week to week.

collocations: to be on a zero-hours contract
note_fr: Notion essentiellement britannique, sans équivalent en droit français, où le contrat à temps partiel doit en principe prévoir une durée de travail. Aux États-Unis, on parlera de « on-call » ou « per diem » work.

def: The default US rule under which either party may end the employment at any time, with or without a reason or notice.

formal.ex: Nothing in this handbook alters the [[employment at will]] relationship between the Company and its employees.

everyday.ex: Remember that our US staff are [[at-will]], so there's no notice period to negotiate.

note_fr: Notion américaine, inconnue en France comme au Royaume-Uni. « At-will » ne veut pas dire sans limites : un licenciement discriminatoire ou prononcé en représailles reste illicite. Évitez de traduire par « à volonté ».

def: A person who works for an employer under a contract of employment in return for pay.

formal.ex: The [[Employee]] shall devote the whole of his or her working time to the business of the Company.

everyday.ex: We've got about two hundred people [[on the payroll]] in France.

informal.ex: He's been [[on the books]] since March, so he's covered by the company health plan.

collocations: to have someone on the payroll
note_fr: « Salaried » n'est pas « salarié » : « a salaried employee » est payé au mois, par opposition à « an hourly employee ». « Staff » est collectif : « a member of staff », jamais « a staff ». « Personnel » est rare et administratif.

def: In UK law, a person who works personally for someone else without being a full employee, and who has some but not all employment rights.

formal.ex: The tribunal held that the claimant was a [[worker]] rather than an employee and was therefore entitled to paid annual leave.

everyday.ex: The drivers are claiming [[worker status]], which would give them holiday pay and the minimum wage.

note_fr: Au Royaume-Uni, « worker » est une catégorie juridique située entre « employee » et « self-employed » : salaire minimum et congés payés, mais pas la protection contre le licenciement abusif. Ni la France ni les États-Unis ne connaissent ce troisième statut ; ailleurs, « worker » veut simplement dire « travailleur ».

def: A self-employed person who provides services to a client under a commercial contract rather than an employment contract.

formal.ex: The Consultant is engaged as an [[independent contractor]] and nothing in this agreement shall create a contract of employment.

everyday.ex: We use a [[freelancer]] for the payroll audits rather than hiring someone.

note_fr: Distinguez « a contract of employment » ou « contract of service » (contrat de travail) de « a contract for services » (contrat de prestation). « Independent » seul ne s'emploie pas comme nom : dites « a contractor », « a freelancer » ou « self-employed ».

fr: salariat déguisé / requalification en contrat de travail
def: Treating someone as self-employed when the reality of the relationship is that of an employee.

formal.ex: The inspector found evidence of [[false self-employment]] and ordered the payment of back contributions.
formal.ex_us: The inspector found evidence of [[worker misclassification]] and ordered the payment of back contributions.

everyday.ex: If he works set hours and reports to our manager, there's a real risk he [[is misclassified]].

collocations: to reclassify a contractor as an employee
note_fr: « Requalification » n'a pas de traduction directe : dites « the contract was reclassified as an employment contract » ou « he was found to be an employee ». Le critère français est le lien de subordination ; au Royaume-Uni on parle de « employment status », aux États-Unis de « misclassification ».

def: A three-party arrangement in which an independent professional is employed by an intermediary company that invoices the client and pays the professional a salary.

formal.ex: The consultant provides her services through [[umbrella company employment]], the umbrella company being her legal employer.
formal.ex_us: The consultant provides her services through an [[employer-of-record arrangement]], the employer of record being her legal employer.

everyday.uk: to work through an umbrella company
everyday.us: to work through an employer of record
everyday.ex: She finds her own clients but [[works through an umbrella company]], so she's technically an employee.
everyday.ex_us: She finds her own clients but [[works through an employer of record]], so she's technically an employee.

note_fr: Les équivalents sont approximatifs : l'« umbrella company » britannique et l'« employer of record » américain reposent sur des logiques proches, mais le portage salarial est un dispositif français encadré par la loi. Gardez le terme français et glosez-le.

explain.written: Portage salarial is a French statutory arrangement under which an autonomous professional is employed by a specialist company that invoices his or her clients and converts the fees into a salary.
explain.spoken: It's a bit like working through an umbrella company: she finds her own clients, but a specialist firm invoices them and pays her a salary.

def: A temporary transfer to another entity or country while remaining employed by the original employer.

formal.ex: During the [[secondment]], the Employee shall remain an employee of the home company.
formal.ex_us: During the [[temporary assignment]], the Employee shall remain an employee of the home company.

everyday.ex: She's [[been seconded to]] the Dublin office for a year.
everyday.ex_us: She's [[been on loan to]] the Dublin office for a year.

note_fr: « Secondment » (accent sur la deuxième syllabe, comme le verbe « to second » /sɪˈkɒnd/) est britannique ; un Américain dira « assignment » ou « loan ». Le détachement au sens du droit européen se dit « posting » : « a posted worker ». « Detachment » est un faux ami (détachement affectif ou militaire).

def: A long-term posting abroad, usually with a specific package and a contract adapted to the host country.

formal.ex: The terms of the [[international assignment]] are set out in the attached assignment letter.

everyday.ex: He [[was posted abroad]] for three years and came back on a local contract.

collocations: the home country and the host country
note_fr: En français, le détaché reste rattaché au contrat et à la sécurité sociale d'origine alors que l'expatrié en sort : l'anglais ne fait pas cette distinction avec deux mots, précisez-la. La prononciation diffère : UK /ekˈspætriət/, US /ekˈspeɪtriət/.

def: A written agreement negotiated between employers and trade unions that sets pay and working conditions for a group of employees.

formal.ex: This contract is governed by [[the applicable collective agreement]], a copy of which is available from Human Resources.
formal.ex_us: This contract is governed by [[the applicable collective bargaining agreement]], a copy of which is available from Human Resources.

everyday.ex: Check [[the industry agreement]] first - it may give a longer notice period than the contract.
everyday.ex_us: Check [[the union contract]] first - it may give a longer notice period than the contract.

collocations: to be covered by a collective agreement
to fall within the scope of the agreement
note_fr: « Convention » est un faux ami (congrès, usage). En France, la convention collective de branche s'applique à presque tous les salariés ; au Royaume-Uni et aux États-Unis, un accord collectif ne couvre que les entreprises où un syndicat est reconnu. Le « CBA » américain est en pratique un accord d'entreprise.

explain.written: The convention collective is a sector-wide collective agreement which, once extended by the government, binds every employer in the industry and supplements the Labour Code.
explain.spoken: In France almost every employee is covered by an industry-wide agreement - it sits on top of the law and often gives better terms than the contract.

def: A French arrangement under which an autonomous employee's working time is counted in days per year rather than in hours.

formal.ex: The Employee's working time is organised under an [[annual working-days arrangement]], as permitted by the applicable collective agreement.

everyday.uk: to be on a days-per-year contract
everyday.us: to be on a days-per-year contract
everyday.ex: Most of our managers [[are on a days-per-year contract]], so we don't track their hours.

collocations: to count working time in days
note_fr: Aucun équivalent direct. Le plus proche est, aux États-Unis, l'« exempt employee » (non soumis aux heures supplémentaires), mais la logique est différente. N'écrivez pas « day package » ni « flat-rate days » sans explication.

explain.written: The forfait jours is a French arrangement, requiring both a collective agreement and the employee's written consent, whereby working time is measured as a fixed number of days per year instead of weekly hours.
explain.spoken: Their time is counted in days per year, not hours - so there's no overtime, but we have to keep an eye on their workload and rest.

def: The employer's power to give instructions, supervise the work and discipline the employee, which defines an employment contract in French law.

formal.ex: The existence of an employment contract depends on a [[relationship of subordination]], whatever name the parties have given to their agreement.

everyday.ex: If he [[is under our control]] day to day, a court will treat him as an employee.

collocations: to work under the direction of
note_fr: « Subordination » et « subordinate » existent, mais sonnent durs dans la conversation : parlez de « control » ou de « direction ». Au Royaume-Uni, les juges examinent « control », « mutuality of obligation » et « personal service » ; aux États-Unis, le « right to control ».

explain.written: Under French law an employment contract is characterised by a relationship of subordination, meaning that the employer has the power to give orders, monitor their execution and sanction any failings.
explain.spoken: What makes someone an employee in France is control: the employer tells them what to do, checks the work and can discipline them.

def: To give someone a job and enter into an employment relationship with them.

formal.ex: The Company agrees [[to engage]] the Employee as Regional Sales Manager.
formal.ex_us: The Company agrees [[to hire]] the Employee as Regional Sales Manager.

everyday.ex: We're [[taking on]] three new consultants in September.
everyday.ex_us: We're [[bringing on]] three new consultants in September.

collocations: to hire someone as a manager
note_fr: « To engage » signifie ici « embaucher » uniquement en style contractuel britannique ; à l'oral, « to engage » veut dire « impliquer ». « A new hire » ou « a new joiner » (UK) désigne la personne recrutée. Évitez « to embauch » et le calque « to make an engagement ».

def: A proposal made by an employer to a chosen candidate to take up a specific job on stated terms.

formal.ex: We are pleased to confirm our [[offer of employment]] on the terms set out below.

everyday.ex: We'd like [[to make her an offer]] before she hears back from the other firm.

collocations: to put an offer in writing
note_fr: « Job offer » est l'offre faite à un candidat retenu ; l'offre d'emploi publiée est « a job advertisement », « a job ad » ou « a job posting » (US), « a vacancy » (UK). « To extend an offer » est très courant aux États-Unis.

def: A letter from the employer confirming the job offer and its main terms.

formal.ex: Please sign and return the enclosed [[letter of offer]] by Friday 12 June.
formal.ex_us: Please sign and return the enclosed [[offer letter]] by Friday, June 12.

everyday.ex: HR will send out the [[offer letter]] as soon as the salary's been approved.

collocations: to send out an offer letter
to sign and return the offer letter
note_fr: Aux États-Unis, l'« offer letter » tient souvent lieu de contrat : beaucoup de salariés n'ont pas d'autre document. En France et au Royaume-Uni, elle précède en général un contrat écrit complet.

def: A job offer that only becomes final once certain conditions, such as references or checks, have been met.

formal.ex: This [[offer is subject to]] the receipt of two satisfactory references and proof of your right to work in the United Kingdom.
formal.ex_us: This [[offer is contingent upon]] the successful completion of a background check and proof of your eligibility to work in the United States.

everyday.ex: It's only a [[conditional offer]] for now - don't hand in your notice until the checks have come back.
everyday.ex_us: It's only a [[contingent offer]] for now - don't give notice until the checks have come back.

collocations: to make an offer conditional on
note_fr: « Subject to » (sous réserve de) est la formule clé ; ne traduisez pas « sous réserve de » par « under reserve of ». Aux États-Unis, on dit plus volontiers « contingent on/upon ».

def: In French practice, a written offer precise enough about the job, pay and start date to commit the employer.

formal.ex: A [[binding offer of employment]] which specifies the position, the remuneration and the start date commits the employer under French law.

everyday.ex: Be careful what you put in that email - in France a [[firm offer]] can be as good as a contract.

collocations: to go back on an offer
to be bound by an offer
note_fr: Ne traduisez pas par « promise of hiring » ou « hiring promise ». Le droit français distingue l'offre de contrat de travail de la promesse unilatérale de contrat, cette dernière valant contrat dès que le candidat l'accepte ; au Royaume-Uni, une offre acceptée forme déjà le contrat, et aux États-Unis l'« at-will » limite fortement la portée d'une telle promesse.

explain.written: Under French case law, a promesse d'embauche that states the position, the remuneration and the start date may bind the employer, so that withdrawing it can amount to an unlawful termination.
explain.spoken: In France, once you've put the job, the salary and the start date in writing, you may already be committed - pulling out can cost you damages.

def: To agree formally to take a job on the terms proposed.

formal.ex: Please confirm in writing that you [[accept the offer]] by signing and returning one copy of this letter.

everyday.ex: She [[said yes]] straight away, so we can stop interviewing.

collocations: to accept an offer in writing
note_fr: Attention à la construction : « to accept an offer », mais « to agree to the terms » (jamais « to accept to do something »). « Acceptance » est le nom ; « acceptation » n'existe pas dans ce sens.

def: To refuse a job offer politely.

formal.ex: After careful consideration, I regret that I must [[decline the offer]].

everyday.ex: He [[turned down]] the offer because the package didn't include a company car.

collocations: to turn an offer down flat
note_fr: « To refuse an offer » est correct mais plus sec ; « to turn down » est le verbe naturel à l'oral. « To decline » se construit directement : « she declined the offer », sans préposition.

def: To cancel a job offer after it has been made.

formal.ex: The Company reserves the right [[to withdraw the offer]] if the references prove unsatisfactory.
formal.ex_us: The Company reserves the right [[to rescind the offer]] if the background check proves unsatisfactory.

everyday.ex: They [[pulled the offer]] two days before he was due to start.

collocations: to withdraw an offer of employment
to go back on an offer
note_fr: « To retire » signifie « prendre sa retraite », jamais « retirer ». Au Royaume-Uni, retirer une offre déjà acceptée constitue une rupture de contrat ; aux États-Unis, « to rescind an offer » est en général possible, sous réserve des règles anti-discrimination.

def: The day on which the employee begins working under the contract.

formal.ex: The Employee's employment shall begin on the [[commencement date]] stated in Schedule 1.

everyday.ex: Can we push her [[start date]] back a week? Her laptop won't be ready.

collocations: to bring the start date forward
to push back the start date
note_fr: Ne dites pas « date of entry » ni « entrance date ». « To push back » = reporter, « to bring forward » = avancer. Notez l'usage : UK « to agree a date », US « to agree on a date ».

def: To begin working in a new job or position.

formal.ex: The Employee shall [[take up her duties]] on 1 September at the Company's head office.

everyday.ex: She [[starts]] on Monday, so let's make sure someone's there to show her round.

note_fr: Pas de « to take one's functions » : « function » désigne en anglais un service de l'entreprise (« the HR function ») ou une réception, pas le poste d'une personne. « To take up » est indispensable ; « to join » (sans « to ») pour « rejoindre l'entreprise ».

fr: vérification du droit de travailler (titre de séjour, autorisation de travail)
def: The employer's legal duty to verify, before employment starts, that a person is allowed to work in the country.

formal.ex: Your employment is conditional upon the satisfactory completion of a [[right-to-work check]].
formal.ex_us: Your employment is conditional upon the satisfactory completion of [[employment eligibility verification]].

everyday.uk: to check someone's right to work
everyday.ex: Don't let him start until we've [[checked his right to work]].
everyday.ex_us: Don't let him start until we've [[verified his work authorization]].

collocations: proof of the right to work
note_fr: Piège majeur : aux États-Unis, « right-to-work » désigne les lois d'État qui interdisent d'imposer l'adhésion à un syndicat, pas le droit de travailler des étrangers. Là-bas, la vérification passe par le formulaire I-9 ; on parle de « work authorization ».

def: Verifications of a candidate's identity, qualifications, work history or record carried out before hiring is confirmed.

formal.ex: The offer remains subject to the satisfactory outcome of [[pre-employment checks]].
formal.ex_us: The offer remains subject to the satisfactory outcome of a [[background check]].

everyday.ex: We always [[take up references]] before we send the contract out.
everyday.ex_us: We always [[check references]] before we send the contract out.

note_fr: « A reference » est la recommandation ; la personne qui la donne est « a referee » (UK) ou « a reference » (US). En France, ces vérifications sont strictement encadrées (lien direct avec le poste, information du candidat), bien plus qu'aux États-Unis où le « background check » est courant.

fr: document écrit récapitulant les conditions essentielles d'emploi (UK)
def: In the UK, the document an employer must give setting out the main terms of employment, such as pay, hours and holiday.

formal.us: written statement of the terms of employment
formal.ex: The employer must provide a [[written statement of employment particulars]] no later than the first day of employment.
formal.ex_us: The employer must provide a [[written statement of the terms of employment]] no later than the first day of employment.

everyday.ex: He never got a contract as such, but he did get a [[written statement]] on day one.

note_fr: Notion britannique : ce n'est pas le contrat lui-même, mais l'information écrite obligatoire sur ses éléments essentiels, due au plus tard le premier jour de travail. « Particulars » signifie ici « mentions, renseignements », pas « particuliers ». Il n'existe pas d'obligation fédérale générale comparable aux États-Unis.

fr: livret d'accueil / règlement et politiques internes
def: A document given to employees that explains the organisation's rules, policies and procedures.

formal.ex: The policies contained in the [[Staff Handbook]] do not form part of your contract of employment.
formal.ex_us: The policies contained in the [[Employee Handbook]] do not create a contract of employment.

everyday.ex: It's all in the [[handbook]] - have a look at the section on expenses.

collocations: to acknowledge receipt of the handbook
note_fr: Ce n'est pas le règlement intérieur français, qui est obligatoire à partir d'un certain effectif et soumis à une procédure légale : traduisez celui-ci par « internal rules » ou « works rules ». Le « handbook » est le plus souvent non contractuel.

def: To prepare the written text of a contract.

formal.ex: The contract shall be [[drafted]] in French, with an English translation provided for information only.

everyday.ex: Can you [[draw up]] the contract today so she can sign before the weekend?

note_fr: « To redact » est un faux ami : il signifie « caviarder, occulter » un passage. « Rédiger » se dit « to draft », « to draw up » ou simplement « to write ». « To establish a contract » est un calque à éviter.

def: The persons or organisations that sign a contract and are bound by it.

formal.ex: This agreement is made between [[the parties]] named below.

everyday.ex: [[Both sides]] need to sign before she can start.

note_fr: On est « a party to a contract » (préposition « to », jamais « of »). Devant un nom défini, les contrats anglais mettent une majuscule : « the Employer », « the Employee », « the Parties ».

def: The official name of the position a person holds in an organisation.

formal.ex: The Employee shall [[be employed as]] Senior Payroll Officer.

everyday.ex: Her [[job title]] is HR Business Partner, but she does a lot of employee relations work.

note_fr: Ne traduisez pas « poste » par « post » dans tous les cas : « position », « role » et « job » sont plus naturels (« post » est surtout britannique et administratif). « Cadre » n'a pas d'équivalent : dites « manager » ou « professional » selon le cas.

def: The tasks and responsibilities that an employee is required to carry out in a job.

formal.ex: The Employee shall perform such [[duties]] as the Company may reasonably assign from time to time.

everyday.ex: Let me run you through [[what the job involves]] before we talk about salary.

note_fr: « Functions » ne désigne pas les fonctions d'une personne en anglais courant : préférez « duties », « responsibilities » ou « role ». La fiche de poste est « a job description » (« a JD » à l'oral).

def: To have someone as your direct manager in the organisation.

formal.ex: The Employee shall [[report to]] the Head of Human Resources or such other person as the Company may designate.

everyday.ex: On paper she reports to Paris, but day to day she [[answers to]] the site manager.

note_fr: « To be attached to » est un calque. « A direct report » est le subordonné direct (N-1) ; le supérieur hiérarchique est « line manager » (UK) ou « supervisor », « manager » (US). « Hierarchy » et surtout « hierarchical superior » sonnent très français.

def: The location where the employee normally carries out the job.

formal.ex: The Employee's [[normal place of work]] shall be the Company's offices in Lyon.
formal.ex_us: The Employee's [[principal place of work]] shall be the Company's offices in Lyon.

everyday.ex: She [[is based in]] Lyon but spends two days a week at the Paris office.

note_fr: Dites « to be based in/at », pas « to be located » pour une personne. Le télétravail se dit « remote work », « working from home » (« WFH ») ; « telework » existe surtout dans les textes officiels, et « home office » désigne la pièce, pas la pratique.

def: The number of hours, and the times of day, that an employee is required to work.

formal.ex: The Employee's [[normal hours of work]] are thirty-five hours per week, Monday to Friday.

everyday.ex: The [[hours]] are nine to five-thirty, with some flexibility if you need it.

note_fr: « Horaire » ne se traduit pas par « hourly » (qui veut dire « à l'heure ») ni par « schedule » dans tous les cas : « working hours » couvre la durée et les horaires. « Timetable » est scolaire ou ferroviaire. Les « 35 heures » : « the 35-hour week ».

def: Everything an employee receives in return for work, including salary, bonuses and other payments.

formal.ex: In consideration of her services, the Employee shall receive a gross annual [[remuneration]] of the amount stated in Schedule 1.
formal.ex_us: In consideration of her services, the Employee shall receive gross annual [[compensation]] in the amount stated in Schedule 1.

everyday.ex: The [[pay]] isn't great, but the pension contributions are generous.

informal.ex: With the bonus on top, it adds up to a pretty decent [[pay packet]].
informal.ex_us: With the bonus on top, it adds up to a pretty decent [[paycheck]].

note_fr: Orthographe : « remuneration », pas « renumeration » (erreur fréquente, même chez les natifs). Aux États-Unis, « compensation » signifie rémunération ; au Royaume-Uni, il évoque plutôt une indemnisation (dommages-intérêts). Brut / net : « gross » / « net » ou « take-home pay ».

def: Things an employee receives from the employer in addition to salary, such as health cover, a pension or a company car.

formal.ex: The Employee shall be entitled to participate in the Company's [[benefits]] schemes, subject to their rules as amended from time to time.
formal.ex_us: The Employee shall be eligible to participate in the Company's [[benefits]] plans, subject to their terms as amended from time to time.

everyday.ex: The salary's about average, but the [[benefits package]] is hard to beat.

informal.ex: Free parking and a gym membership are nice [[perks]], but they won't keep people for long.

note_fr: « Advantages » ne s'emploie pas dans ce sens. Attention aussi : au Royaume-Uni, « to be on benefits » signifie toucher des allocations de l'État. Avantage en nature : « benefit in kind » (UK), « fringe benefit » (US). Mutuelle : « health cover » (UK), « health insurance » (US).

def: The paid days off work that an employee is entitled to each year.

formal.ex: The Employee is entitled to five weeks' [[paid annual leave]] in each holiday year.
formal.ex_us: The Employee is entitled to five weeks of [[paid vacation]] in each calendar year.

everyday.ex: How much [[holiday]] have you got left this year?
everyday.ex_us: How much [[vacation]] do you have left this year?

note_fr: UK « holiday », US « vacation » ; « holidays » aux États-Unis désigne les jours fériés (UK « bank holidays » ou « public holidays »). « Congé » en général se dit « leave » : « sick leave », « parental leave ». « PTO » (US) regroupe souvent congés et jours de maladie. Il n'existe pas de congés payés légaux au niveau fédéral américain.

fr: conditions d'emploi / clauses et conditions du contrat
def: All the rights and obligations that apply to a job, such as pay, hours, holiday and notice.

formal.ex: Your [[terms and conditions of employment]] are set out in this letter and in the attached schedule.

everyday.ex: The [[terms]] are pretty standard - nothing you'd need a lawyer for.

collocations: under the terms of the contract
note_fr: « Terms » = les stipulations du contrat ; « term » au singulier = la durée (« the term of the contract ») : ne les confondez pas. « T&Cs » est l'abréviation courante. « Conditions » seul évoque plutôt les conditions matérielles de travail.

def: An initial period during which the employer assesses the new employee and either party can end the contract more easily.

formal.ex: The first four months of employment shall constitute a [[probationary period]], during which either party may terminate the contract on short notice.

everyday.ex: He's still [[on probation]], so let's give him feedback now rather than wait.

note_fr: « Trial period » se comprend mais « probation » est le terme usuel ; « essay » et « test period » sont à proscrire. En France, la période d'essai doit être prévue expressément par le contrat et sa durée maximale dépend de la catégorie du salarié ; au Royaume-Uni et aux États-Unis, elle relève surtout de la pratique de l'entreprise.

explain.written: The période d'essai is a probationary period which must be expressly stipulated in the contract, whose maximum length is set by law according to the employee's category, and during which either party may end the contract without giving reasons, subject to a short notice.
explain.spoken: It's the French probation period: it has to be written into the contract, the law caps how long it can last, and either side can end things quickly while it's running.

def: To lengthen the initial assessment period because more time is needed to evaluate the employee.

formal.ex: The Company may [[extend the probationary period]] once, with the Employee's express written agreement.

everyday.ex: We'd rather [[extend his probation]] by a couple of months than let him go now.

collocations: to extend probation by three months
note_fr: En anglais on « extends » une période d'essai ; « to renew probation » surprendrait un natif. Précisez la règle française à vos interlocuteurs, qui pensent qu'une simple décision de l'employeur suffit.

explain.written: Under French law the probationary period may be renewed once only, provided that the applicable industry-wide agreement allows it, the contract provides for it and the employee expressly agrees.
explain.spoken: In France you can only extend probation once, and only if the industry agreement and the contract allow it - and the employee has to agree in writing.

fr: valider sa période d'essai / être confirmé(e) dans son poste
def: To complete the probationary period successfully and continue in the job.

formal.us: to be confirmed in the position
formal.ex: On successful completion of the probationary period, the Employee shall [[be confirmed in post]].
formal.ex_us: On successful completion of the probationary period, the Employee shall [[be confirmed in the position]].

everyday.ex: She [[passed probation]] with flying colours, so the longer notice period now applies.

note_fr: « To validate » est un calque : on « passes » ou « completes » sa période d'essai. Pour la rupture pendant l'essai, dites « she didn't pass probation » ou « we ended his probation » ; « to break the trial period » ne se dit pas.

def: The amount of time an employee has worked for the same employer without a break.

formal.ex: For the purposes of this clause, the Employee's period of [[continuous service]] began on 3 January 2019.
formal.ex_us: For the purposes of this section, the Employee's [[length of service]] began on January 3, 2019.

everyday.uk: to have been with the company for
everyday.us: to have been with the company for
everyday.ex: She's [[been with the company for]] twelve years, so her notice period is much longer.

note_fr: « Ancientness » n'existe pas. Au Royaume-Uni, « seniority » désigne surtout le rang hiérarchique ; l'ancienneté est « length of service » ou, en droit, « continuous employment ». Aux États-Unis, « seniority » signifie bien ancienneté, surtout en contexte syndical. « Tenure » se dit aussi (US).

def: A numbered section of a contract dealing with one particular point.

formal.ex: The restrictions in [[clause]] 14 shall continue to apply after the termination of this agreement.
formal.ex_us: The restrictions in [[Section]] 14 shall continue to apply after the termination of this agreement.

everyday.ex: There's a [[clause]] in his contract that says he can be moved to any site in France.

note_fr: On dit « under clause 5 » ou « pursuant to clause 5 », pas « according to the clause 5 » (pas d'article devant un numéro). Les contrats américains parlent plutôt de « Section » ; « article » est possible mais « provision » est le mot générique pour « stipulation ».

def: To state something clearly and in an organised way in a written document.

formal.ex: Clause 8 [[provides that]] the Employee may be required to travel within the European Union.

everyday.ex: What does the contract actually [[say]] about working from home?

note_fr: « To stipulate » existe mais reste rare ; « to provide that » et « to set out » sont les verbes naturels. Attention : « to foresee » (prévoir l'avenir) ne convient pas - « the contract foresees » est un calque. « To provide for » + nom, « to provide that » + proposition.

def: A contract term allowing the employer to change the employee's place of work within a defined area.

formal.ex: The [[mobility clause]] must define precisely the geographical area within which the Employee may be transferred.
formal.ex_us: The [[relocation clause]] must define precisely the geographic area within which the Employee may be transferred.

everyday.ex: Under her contract she can [[be asked to relocate]] anywhere in the Paris region.

note_fr: En droit français, la clause doit délimiter précisément sa zone géographique et ne peut pas être étendue unilatéralement. Au Royaume-Uni, la « mobility clause » doit être appliquée de façon raisonnable ; aux États-Unis, l'employeur peut en général imposer une mutation sans clause.

def: A contract term that forbids the employee from disclosing or misusing the employer's confidential information.

formal.ex: The Employee's [[duty of confidentiality]] shall continue without limit in time after the termination of employment.

everyday.ex: You're expected [[to keep client data confidential]], even after you've left.

note_fr: « Confidential » se construit avec « keep » : « to keep it confidential ». « To divulge » existe mais « to disclose » est le verbe juridique. Secret des affaires : « trade secrets ». L'« NDA » est un accord distinct, très courant aux États-Unis.

def: A contract term that prevents an employee from working for a competitor or setting up a competing business for a period after leaving.

formal.ex: The [[non-competition covenant]] shall apply for twelve months following the termination date.
formal.ex_us: The [[covenant not to compete]] shall apply for twelve months following the termination date.

everyday.ex: He can't join them until next spring - he's got a twelve-month [[non-compete]].

collocations: to be bound by a non-compete
to release someone from a non-compete
note_fr: Différence de fond : en France, la clause n'est valable que si elle est limitée dans le temps et l'espace, justifiée par les intérêts légitimes de l'entreprise et assortie d'une contrepartie financière. Au Royaume-Uni, aucune contrepartie n'est exigée mais la clause doit être raisonnable ; aux États-Unis, tout dépend de l'État (la Californie les interdit pour l'essentiel).

fr: clause de non-sollicitation (de clients ou de salariés)
def: A contract term forbidding a former employee from approaching the employer's clients or staff for a set period.

formal.ex: Under the [[non-solicitation covenant]], the Employee shall not approach any client with whom she dealt in the twelve months before leaving.

everyday.ex: She's free to work for a competitor, but she can't [[poach]] our clients or our people.

note_fr: « To solicit » signifie ici « démarcher », mais attention : hors contexte, « soliciting » évoque le racolage. À l'oral, « to poach » (débaucher, littéralement braconner) est le mot juste. Distinguez la non-sollicitation de clients et celle de salariés (« non-poaching »).

def: A contract term that forbids the employee from doing any other paid work during the employment.

formal.ex: By virtue of the [[exclusivity of service]] clause, the Employee shall not engage in any other professional activity without the Company's prior written consent.

everyday.ex: Her contract says she can't [[have a second job]] without clearing it with us first.

informal.ex: He was [[moonlighting]] for a competitor at weekends, which is a clear breach.

note_fr: En France, la clause doit être justifiée par la nature des fonctions et proportionnée, et elle est en principe exclue pour les temps partiels. Au Royaume-Uni, elle est inopposable dans les contrats zéro heure. « To moonlight » = avoir un second emploi, souvent non déclaré à l'employeur.

fr: cession des droits de propriété intellectuelle
def: A contract term transferring to the employer the rights in what the employee creates in the course of the job.

formal.ex: The Employee hereby [[assigns]] to the Company all intellectual property rights in any work created in the course of her employment.

everyday.ex: Anything you develop on the job [[belongs to the company]] - that's standard.

collocations: to assign rights to the employer
note_fr: « Assignment » = cession (et aussi « mission ») ; « cession » en anglais est rare et concerne surtout les territoires. Le régime diffère : en France, l'auteur salarié reste en principe titulaire de ses droits sauf cession expresse (avec des règles propres aux logiciels et aux inventions) ; aux États-Unis, la doctrine du « work made for hire » attribue l'œuvre à l'employeur.

fr: dispense de préavis rémunérée avec maintien des obligations (« garden leave »)
def: A period during notice when the employee stays at home on full pay, remains bound by the contract and may not work for anyone else.

formal.ex: The Company may place the Employee on [[garden leave]] for all or part of the notice period.

everyday.ex: They've put him on [[gardening leave]] for three months so he can't take the clients with him.
everyday.ex_us: They've put him on [[garden leave]] for three months so he can't take the clients with him.

collocations: to put someone on garden leave
note_fr: Notion essentiellement britannique (« gardening leave » à l'oral), connue aux États-Unis surtout dans la finance. Ce n'est pas la dispense de préavis française : le contrat continue, le salarié reste tenu à la loyauté et ne peut pas commencer ailleurs.

def: A contract term requiring an employee to reimburse training costs if he or she leaves within a set period after the training.

formal.ex: Under the [[training costs repayment clause]], the sum repayable decreases by one twenty-fourth for each complete month of service.
formal.ex_us: Under the [[training repayment agreement]], the sum repayable decreases by one twenty-fourth for each complete month of service.

everyday.ex: If she leaves within two years, she'll have [[to pay back]] part of the course fees.

collocations: to recover the cost of training
note_fr: Pas de traduction figée : évitez « forfeit clause » ou « training penalty ». En France, la clause n'est valable que si la formation dépasse les obligations légales ou conventionnelles de l'employeur, si le montant est proportionné et si elle ne prive pas le salarié de sa faculté de démissionner.

explain.written: A clause de dédit-formation is a French contractual clause under which an employee who resigns within a specified period after employer-funded training must repay a proportionate share of its cost.
explain.spoken: It's a training payback clause: if we fund an expensive course and the person resigns soon afterwards, they owe us part of the cost.

fr: clause de restitution (de bonus ou de primes)
def: A contract term allowing the employer to recover money already paid, typically a bonus, if certain events occur.

formal.ex: Any bonus paid under this scheme is subject to the [[clawback provision]] in clause 9.

everyday.ex: If he leaves within a year, they can [[claw back]] the sign-on bonus.

note_fr: Terme propre à la rémunération variable, courant dans la finance. Prudence en France : les sanctions pécuniaires sont interdites et une telle clause n'est admise que dans des limites étroites. « To claw back » se sépare : « to claw the money back ».

fr: clause de variation / de révision unilatérale
def: A contract term reserving the employer's right to change certain terms without a new agreement.

formal.uk: to reserve the right to vary
formal.us: to reserve the right to modify
formal.ex: The Company [[reserves the right to vary]] the Employee's duties and place of work on reasonable notice.
formal.ex_us: The Company [[reserves the right to modify]] the Employee's duties and place of work on reasonable notice.

everyday.ex: There's a [[flexibility clause]] in the contract, but I wouldn't rely on it to cut anyone's pay.

collocations: to rely on a variation clause
note_fr: En droit français, une clause par laquelle l'employeur se réserve de modifier unilatéralement un élément essentiel (rémunération, durée du travail) est sans effet. Au Royaume-Uni, ces clauses sont interprétées strictement ; aux États-Unis, l'employeur « at-will » peut en général modifier les conditions pour l'avenir.

def: A contract term stating that the written document contains everything the parties have agreed and replaces earlier discussions.

formal.ex: By virtue of the [[entire agreement clause]], this contract supersedes all previous arrangements between the parties.
formal.ex_us: By virtue of the [[integration clause]], this contract supersedes all prior arrangements between the parties.

everyday.ex: The signed contract [[replaces anything agreed before]], so that email about the bonus doesn't count.

note_fr: Trois noms pour la même clause : « entire agreement clause » (UK), « integration clause » ou « merger clause » (US). Le verbe clé est « to supersede » (remplacer, avec un s : pas « supercede »).

def: A contract term providing that if one provision is invalid, the rest of the contract remains in force.

formal.ex: Any provision held to be invalid shall [[be severed from]] this agreement, and the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect.

everyday.uk: the rest of the contract still stands
everyday.us: the rest of the contract still stands
everyday.ex: Even if the court throws out the non-compete, [[the rest of the contract still stands]].

collocations: to remain in full force and effect
note_fr: « To sever » /ˈsevə/ (retrancher) ne se prononce pas comme « severe » /sɪˈvɪə/. « Nullité partielle » se rend par « severance » d'une clause - à ne pas confondre avec « severance pay » (indemnité de départ).

def: The national or state law that the parties or the rules designate to interpret and regulate the contract.

formal.ex: This contract shall [[be governed by]] and construed in accordance with French law.

everyday.ex: She's based in London, but her contract [[comes under]] French law.

collocations: to be construed in accordance with
note_fr: « Applicable law » se dit aussi, mais « governing law » est le titre habituel de la clause. « To construe » = interpréter (un texte). Aux États-Unis, la loi applicable est celle d'un État (« the laws of the State of New York »), pas une loi « américaine ». Le choix de loi ne prive pas le salarié des règles impératives protectrices.

def: The power of a particular court to hear a dispute, or the territory in which a legal system applies.

formal.ex: The courts of France shall [[have exclusive jurisdiction]] over any dispute arising out of this contract.

everyday.ex: Any dispute would [[go to]] the French labour court, not an English tribunal.
everyday.ex_us: Any dispute would [[go to]] the French labor court, not a US court.

collocations: to submit to the jurisdiction of
note_fr: « Jurisdiction » ne signifie pas « juridiction » au sens de tribunal (« a court », « a tribunal ») : c'est la compétence, ou le pays dont le droit s'applique (« in other jurisdictions »). Le conseil de prud'hommes : « the French labour court » ; au Royaume-Uni, « employment tribunal ». Aux États-Unis, la clause s'appelle « forum selection clause ».

fr: clause de notification (modalités d'envoi des notifications)
def: A contract term specifying how formal communications between the parties must be sent and when they are treated as received.

formal.ex: Any [[notice served]] under this agreement shall be in writing and delivered by hand or sent by recorded delivery.
formal.ex_us: Any [[notice served]] under this agreement shall be in writing and delivered by hand or sent by certified mail.

everyday.ex: You need [[to notify her in writing]] - a phone call isn't enough under the contract.

note_fr: « To notify » est transitif direct : « to notify someone of something », jamais « to notify to someone ». La lettre recommandée avec accusé de réception : « recorded delivery » ou « signed for » (UK), « certified mail, return receipt requested » (US). « Notice » peut aussi signifier préavis : le contexte tranche.

def: Without affecting or limiting another right or provision.

formal.ex: [[Without prejudice to]] clause 12, the Company may suspend the Employee on full pay pending an investigation.

everyday.ex: We can pay the bonus now [[without affecting]] her right to claim the rest later.

collocations: without prejudice to any other rights
note_fr: « Prejudice » est un faux ami : il signifie d'abord « préjugé » ; le préjudice subi se dit « harm », « loss » ou « damage ». Au Royaume-Uni, « without prejudice » en tête d'un courrier signifie aussi que son contenu ne pourra pas être produit en justice (négociation transactionnelle). Aux États-Unis, « dismissed with/without prejudice » concerne le rejet d'une action.

def: In spite of; used to say that a provision applies even if another provision appears to say otherwise.

formal.ex: [[Notwithstanding]] clause 4, the Employee may be required to work at any of the Company's sites in France.

everyday.ex: [[Despite]] what clause 4 says, she can be asked to work at another site.

note_fr: Mot purement rédactionnel : ne l'employez jamais à l'oral. Il indique quelle clause l'emporte ; son symétrique est « subject to » (sous réserve de). « Notwithstanding the foregoing » = nonobstant ce qui précède.

def: A written document, signed by both parties, that changes one or more terms of an existing contract.

formal.ex: This [[amendment]] forms an integral part of the employment contract dated 2 May 2022.
formal.ex_us: This [[amendment]] forms an integral part of the employment contract dated May 2, 2022.

everyday.uk: to put a change in writing
everyday.us: to put a change in writing
everyday.ex: If we're changing her hours, we need [[to put the change in writing]] and get her to sign.

note_fr: « Avenant » n'a pas d'équivalent unique : « amendment » (modifie le texte), « addendum » (ajoute), ou au Royaume-Uni « variation letter ». « Rider » concerne surtout les assurances. Ne dites pas « an avenant » sans l'expliquer.

explain.written: An avenant is a written amendment to the employment contract which, under French law, must be signed by both parties whenever an essential term such as pay, working time or job content is changed.
explain.spoken: An avenant is just a signed amendment to the contract - in France you need one every time you change something essential like pay or hours.

def: To change one or more of the agreed terms of a contract.

formal.ex: The employer may not [[vary the contract]] without the Employee's express agreement.
formal.ex_us: The employer may not [[modify the contract]] without the Employee's express agreement.

everyday.ex: We can't just [[change her contract]] - she has to agree to it.

note_fr: Au Royaume-Uni, le terme juridique est « variation of contract » ; un Américain dira « modification » ou « amendment ». En France, toute modification d'un élément essentiel du contrat exige l'accord du salarié, dont le refus n'est pas fautif.

fr: simple changement des conditions de travail
def: In French law, a change the employer may impose without the employee's agreement because it does not affect an essential term of the contract.

formal.ex: A mere [[change in working conditions]] falls within the employer's managerial prerogative and does not require the Employee's consent.

everyday.uk: a change we can make without consent
everyday.us: a change we can make without consent
everyday.ex: Moving her start time by half an hour is [[a change we can make without consent]] - it isn't a contract change.

collocations: an essential term of the contract
to fall within the employer's discretion
note_fr: La distinction « modification du contrat » / « changement des conditions de travail » est propre au droit français. Les Britanniques raisonnent en « contractual » / « non-contractual terms » ; expliquez toujours les deux branches et leurs conséquences.

explain.written: French law distinguishes a variation of the contract, which requires the employee's consent, from a mere change in working conditions, which the employer may impose by virtue of its managerial prerogative and which the employee may not refuse without being at fault.
explain.spoken: In France there are two kinds of change: the ones that touch the contract itself, where you need the employee's agreement, and the day-to-day ones the employer can simply decide.

def: To agree formally to something that is proposed.

formal.ex: No change shall be made to the Employee's remuneration without her [[express written consent]].

everyday.ex: She's [[agreed to]] the new hours, so we just need her signature.

note_fr: « To agree » : pas de « to be agree » ni « I am agree ». Construction : « to agree to a change », « to agree with someone », « to agree on a date ». « Consent » /kənˈsent/ est accentué sur la seconde syllabe ; « express » (exprès) s'oppose à « implied » (tacite).

def: A period during which the main obligations of work and pay are paused while the contract itself continues to exist.

formal.ex: The employment contract shall [[be suspended]] for the duration of the parental leave.

everyday.ex: While she [[is on leave]], the contract's still in place - she just isn't working or being paid by us.

note_fr: Piège : en anglais, « to suspend an employee » ou « she's been suspended » évoque presque toujours une mise à pied (disciplinaire ou conservatoire). Pour la suspension du contrat à la française (maladie, maternité, congé parental), dites plutôt « she is on leave » et glosez.

explain.written: In French law the employment contract is said to be suspended when, during events such as sick leave, maternity leave or a strike, the duties to work and to pay cease temporarily while the contract remains in existence.
explain.spoken: In France we say the contract is 'suspended' when someone's off sick or on parental leave - it just means the contract is on hold, not that they're in any trouble.

def: To make a contract continue for a further period after it would otherwise have ended.

formal.ex: The fixed-term contract may [[be renewed]] on the conditions laid down by the applicable collective agreement.

everyday.ex: We'd like [[to keep him on]] for another six months if the budget allows.

collocations: to renew a contract for a further term
note_fr: « To extend » (prolonger) et « to renew » (renouveler) sont proches ; « to keep someone on » est l'expression naturelle à l'oral. « To reconduct » n'existe pas : la tacite reconduction se dit « automatic renewal » ou « the contract rolls over ».

fr: arriver à échéance / à son terme
def: To come to an end because the agreed period has finished.

formal.ex: [[On expiry of]] the fixed term, the contract shall end automatically without notice.
formal.ex_us: [[Upon expiration of]] the fixed term, the contract shall end automatically without notice.

everyday.ex: His contract [[runs out]] at the end of June, so we need to decide soon.

note_fr: UK « expiry », US « expiration ». « Échéance » ne se traduit pas par « deadline » ici (date limite pour faire quelque chose) mais par « end date » ou « expiry ». « Term » = durée du contrat, d'où « the end of the term ».

term.uk: to convert to a permanent contract
term.us: to convert to a permanent contract

def: To change a temporary employment relationship into one with no end date.

formal.uk: to be deemed to be permanent
formal.us: to be deemed to be permanent
formal.ex: Where the employee continues to work after the end of the fixed term, the contract shall [[be deemed to be permanent]].

everyday.ex: She's done so well that we've decided [[to make her permanent]].

informal.ex: He started as a temp and [[went perm]] after six months.

collocations: to become permanent by operation of law
note_fr: « To be deemed » = être réputé. En France, la poursuite du travail après le terme du CDD le transforme en CDI, et le juge peut aussi requalifier un CDD irrégulier : dites « the contract was reclassified as permanent ». Au Royaume-Uni, des contrats à durée déterminée successifs peuvent aussi devenir permanents au bout d'un certain temps ; rien de tel aux États-Unis.

fr: transfert d'entreprise (transfert automatique des contrats de travail)
def: The sale or handover of a business or service, as a result of which the employees' contracts pass automatically to the new employer in Europe.

formal.ex: In the event of a [[transfer of an undertaking]], the contracts of employment shall transfer automatically to the transferee.
formal.ex_us: In the event of a [[business transfer]], French law provides that the employment contracts transfer automatically to the buyer.

everyday.ex: The catering staff will [[transfer under TUPE]] when the new contractor takes over.
everyday.ex_us: In France the catering staff will [[transfer automatically]] when the new contractor takes over.

informal.ex: About forty of us [[were TUPE'd across]] when the contract changed hands.
informal.ex_us: About forty of us [[moved across]] when the contract changed hands.

note_fr: « TUPE » (prononcé /ˈtjuːpi/) désigne la réglementation britannique issue du droit européen, comme le transfert automatique des contrats en France. Aux États-Unis, rien de tel : en cas de cession d'actifs, l'acquéreur choisit en principe qui il réembauche. « Undertaking » = entreprise au sens du droit européen, mais aussi « engagement ».

def: To start to apply and produce legal effects.

formal.ex: This amendment shall [[come into force]] on the date of its signature by both parties.
formal.ex_us: This amendment shall [[take effect]] on the date of its signature by both parties.

everyday.ex: The new salary [[kicks in]] on the first of next month.

note_fr: « To enter in vigour » est un calque. « With effect from » (UK) et « effective » + date (US : « effective March 1 ») sont les formules usuelles. « To kick in » est familier mais très courant à l'oral.

def: To act in accordance with a rule, a term of a contract or a legal requirement.

formal.ex: The Employee shall [[comply with]] all Company policies in force from time to time.

everyday.ex: As long as both sides [[stick to]] the contract, there shouldn't be a problem.

note_fr: « To respect a contract » est un calque : en anglais on « respects » une personne, on « complies with », « abides by » ou « honours » (US « honors ») une obligation. Le nom est « compliance », d'où « compliance officer ».

def: To make something take effect from a date earlier than the date on which it is agreed or signed.

formal.ex: The salary increase shall apply [[with retroactive effect from]] 1 January.

everyday.ex: They've agreed [[to backdate]] her pay rise to January.
everyday.ex_us: They've agreed [[to backdate]] her raise to January.

note_fr: « To backdate a pay rise » est parfaitement légitime (effet rétroactif convenu) ; « to backdate a document » (y porter une fausse date) peut constituer une fraude : ne confondez pas. UK « retrospective » ou « retroactive », US « retroactive » ; UK « pay rise », US « raise ».

def: The length of time between telling the other party that the contract will end and the date it actually ends.

formal.ex: Either party may terminate this contract by giving the other the [[period of notice]] specified in clause 15.

everyday.ex: She's on three months' [[notice]], so she can't start with us before April.

collocations: a notice period of one month
note_fr: Notez l'apostrophe : « three months' notice », « one month's notice ». « Preavis » et « prior notice » ne désignent pas le préavis de rupture. Aux États-Unis, il n'y a en général pas de préavis légal : « two weeks' notice » est un usage de courtoisie. « At short notice » (UK) / « on short notice » (US) = au dernier moment.

def: To tell your employer formally that you are leaving your job.

formal.ex: I hereby [[tender my resignation]] from my position as Finance Manager, with effect from 31 March.
formal.ex_us: I hereby [[tender my resignation]] from my position as Finance Manager, effective March 31.

everyday.ex: He [[handed in his notice]] this morning - he's going to a competitor.
everyday.ex_us: He [[gave notice]] this morning - he's going to a competitor.

informal.ex: She [[quit]] after a row with her manager and didn't even work her notice.
informal.ex_us: She [[quit]] after a fight with her manager and didn't even work out her two weeks.

note_fr: Trois pièges : « to dismiss » signifie licencier, pas démissionner ; « to demission » n'existe pas ; « to resign » n'est pas « résilier » (« to terminate »). On dit « to resign from a job » ou « to resign as director ». « To walk out » = partir du jour au lendemain, sans préavis.

def: A sum paid to an employee instead of having him or her work the notice period.

formal.ex: The Company may terminate the employment with immediate effect by making a [[payment in lieu of notice]].
formal.ex_us: The Company may terminate the employment with immediate effect by providing [[pay in lieu of notice]].

everyday.ex: We'd rather [[pay him in lieu]] than have him in the office for three months.
everyday.ex_us: We'd rather [[pay out his notice]] than have him in the office for three months.

note_fr: « In lieu of » = au lieu de, à la place de ; prononcez /ljuː/ ou /luː/, pas à la française. L'abréviation britannique est « PILON ». Aux États-Unis, la notion est moins courante puisqu'il n'y a généralement pas de préavis obligatoire.

def: To continue working normally until the end of the notice period.

formal.ex: The Employee shall be required [[to work the notice period]] unless the Company decides otherwise.

everyday.ex: She's offered [[to work her notice]] in full so she can hand everything over properly.
everyday.ex_us: She's offered [[to work out her notice]] in full so she can hand everything off properly.

informal.ex: He just [[walked out]] on Friday - no notice, no handover, nothing.

collocations: to be released from one's notice
note_fr: « To execute one's notice » est un calque. UK « to work one's notice », US plutôt « to work out one's notice » ou « to work one's two weeks ». Passation : « handover » (UK), « handoff » ou « transition » (US).

def: To bring a contract to an end.

formal.ex: Either party may [[terminate]] this contract by giving not less than three months' written notice.

everyday.ex: They [[ended]] his contract during probation.

note_fr: « To terminate » ne veut pas dire « terminer une tâche » (« to finish », « to complete »). « To resign » n'est pas « résilier ». Aux États-Unis, « he was terminated » signifie « il a été licencié » ; au Royaume-Uni, « termination » reste un terme neutre couvrant toute fin de contrat. « To break a contract » veut dire le violer, pas le rompre.

def: To end someone's employment by decision of the employer.

formal.ex: The Company may [[dismiss]] the Employee without notice in the event of gross misconduct.
formal.ex_us: The Company may [[terminate]] the Employee without notice in the event of gross misconduct.

everyday.ex: We had [[to let him go]] after the third warning.

informal.ex: He got [[sacked]] for fiddling his expenses.
informal.ex_us: He got [[fired]] for padding his expenses.

note_fr: « To dismiss » = licencier, jamais démissionner. « To license » = accorder une licence. « To let someone go » est l'euphémisme courant des deux côtés de l'Atlantique. Le licenciement économique est « redundancy » (UK) ou « layoff » (US) : « to make someone redundant » / « to lay someone off ». Aux États-Unis, le terme formel courant est « to terminate » ; « to discharge » se rencontre surtout dans les textes juridiques (« wrongful discharge »).

def: Ending a fixed-term contract before the date on which it was due to finish.

formal.ex: [[Early termination]] of a fixed-term contract is permitted only in the cases provided for by law.

everyday.ex: We can't just [[end her contract early]] because the project's finished ahead of schedule.

collocations: before the end of the term
note_fr: « Anticipated » est un faux ami : « anticipated termination » signifierait « rupture prévue, attendue ». En France, le CDD ne peut être rompu avant son terme que dans des cas limités (accord des parties, faute grave, force majeure, embauche en CDI...) ; les contrats britanniques contiennent souvent, eux, une clause de préavis ou « break clause ».

def: A failure by one party to do what the contract requires.

formal.ex: An employee who discloses such information shall [[be in breach of]] this agreement.

everyday.ex: If she starts with a competitor next week, she'll [[be breaking her contract]].

collocations: to sue for breach of contract
note_fr: « Breach » /briːtʃ/ rime avec « teach ». « Violation » se dit plutôt d'une loi ou d'un règlement (surtout US). « A material breach » est un manquement grave ; au Royaume-Uni, le manquement de l'employeur justifiant le départ du salarié est un « repudiatory breach » (« constructive dismissal »).

def: To be legally obliged to respect a contract, clause or rule.

formal.ex: The Employee shall continue [[to be bound by]] clauses 12 to 14 after the termination of this agreement.

everyday.ex: He's [[tied to]] a twelve-month non-compete, so he can't join them yet.

note_fr: « Bound » est le participe de « to bind » (bind, bound, bound) ; ne le confondez pas avec « bound to » + verbe (« he's bound to refuse » = il va forcément refuser) ni avec « bound for » (à destination de). L'adjectif est « binding » : « a legally binding contract ».

fr: opposable / dont on peut obtenir l'exécution en justice
def: Capable of being upheld and applied by a court.

formal.ex: A non-compete covenant is [[enforceable]] only in so far as it protects a legitimate business interest.

everyday.ex: I doubt that clause would [[stand up in court]] - it's far too wide.

note_fr: « Opposable » n'existe pas en anglais juridique courant : dites « enforceable against someone » ou « binding on someone ». « To enforce » = faire exécuter, faire respecter ; ne traduisez pas par « to reinforce » (renforcer).

def: Having no legal effect at all, as if it had never existed.

formal.ex: Any clause purporting to exclude this right shall be [[null and void]].

everyday.ex: A probation clause that isn't in the signed contract is simply [[invalid]] in France.

informal.uk: not worth the paper it's written on
informal.us: not worth the paper it's written on
informal.ex: Without any compensation, that non-compete is [[not worth the paper it's written on]].

note_fr: « Null » ne s'emploie presque jamais seul dans ce sens : dites « void », « invalid » ou « null and void ». Distinguez « void » (nul dès l'origine) et « voidable » (annulable à la demande d'une partie). « Nullity » est rare ; « null » n'a rien à voir avec « nul » au sens de « mauvais ».

def: To give up a right or a claim voluntarily, or to decide not to enforce it.

formal.ex: The Company may [[waive]] the non-competition covenant by written notice given within fifteen days of termination.

everyday.ex: She's happy [[to give up]] her notice period if it means she can start sooner.

note_fr: « To waive » /weɪv/ se prononce comme « to wave » (saluer) : attention à l'orthographe. « To renounce » est beaucoup plus solennel (un titre, une nationalité). Le nom est « waiver » ; « to waive a fee » = ne pas facturer des frais.

def: To have a legal or contractual right to receive or do something.

formal.ex: The Employee shall [[be entitled to]] twenty-five days' paid leave per year.

everyday.ex: You [[get]] twenty-five days' holiday a year, plus bank holidays.
everyday.ex_us: You [[get]] twenty-five days of vacation a year, plus public holidays.

note_fr: « To have the right to » est correct mais moins idiomatique que « to be entitled to ». Ne confondez pas « entitled » (qui a droit à) et « eligible » (qui remplit les conditions pour y prétendre). Autre sens : « a report entitled... » (intitulé) ; et « he's so entitled » est péjoratif (il croit que tout lui est dû).

fr: être soumis(e) à / sous réserve de
def: To be governed by a rule, or to depend on a condition being met.

formal.ex: [[Subject to]] clause 6, the Employee's salary shall be reviewed annually.

everyday.ex: The bonus [[depends on]] you still being with us at the end of the year.

collocations: to be subject to French law
note_fr: Deux sens à distinguer : « to be subject to French law » (être soumis à) et « subject to approval » (sous réserve de). L'adjectif s'accentue sur la première syllabe /ˈsʌbdʒɪkt/, le verbe « to subject » sur la seconde /səbˈdʒekt/. « Submitted to » est un calque.

def: Later in this document; used to introduce the short name by which a party or thing will be called.

formal.ex: Clarté Conseil SAS, [[hereinafter referred to as]] 'the Company', whose registered office is in Nantes.

everyday.ex: The French entity, [[which we'll call]] the Company from now on, is the employer.

note_fr: Mot de pure rédaction contractuelle. Le style moderne (« plain English ») le remplace souvent par une simple parenthèse : Clarté Conseil SAS (« the Company »). À reconnaître, pas à dire.

def: By means of this document or this statement; used to show that the words themselves perform a legal act.

formal.ex: The Employee [[hereby]] acknowledges receipt of a copy of the internal rules.

everyday.ex: I [[confirm]] that I've received a copy of the internal rules.

note_fr: « Hereby » se place entre le sujet et le verbe et s'accentue sur la seconde syllabe. Réservé aux contrats et aux attestations : dans un e-mail, « I hereby inform you » est pompeux ; écrivez « I'm writing to let you know » ou « I confirm ». « By the present » est un calque.

def: Of the thing just mentioned; a drafting word used to avoid repeating a noun.

formal.ex: The Employee shall return the laptop and any copies of the files stored on it, or any part [[thereof]], on the last day of employment.

everyday.ex: You need to give back the laptop and the files, or whatever part [[of it]] you still have.

note_fr: Clé de lecture : « here- » renvoie au présent document (« hereof » = des présentes, « herein » = dans le présent contrat, « hereto » = aux présentes), « there- » à la chose qui vient d'être citée (« thereof », « therein », « thereafter »). À comprendre plutôt qu'à employer.

def: To write your name on a document to show that you agree to it.

formal.ex: This agreement has been [[executed]] by the parties on the date stated at the beginning of it.

everyday.ex: Could you [[sign]] both copies and send one back to me?

informal.uk: to sign on the dotted line
informal.us: to sign on the dotted line
informal.ex: Don't hand in your notice until you've [[signed on the dotted line]].

note_fr: « To execute a contract » signifie le signer en bonne et due forme, pas l'exécuter (« to perform a contract »). Le « g » de « sign » est muet /saɪn/ mais se prononce dans « signature » /ˈsɪɡnətʃə/ et « signatory ». On signe « a contract », sans préposition.

def: To give formal approval to something so that it can go ahead.

formal.ex: Any amendment to the remuneration package must be [[approved]] by the Remuneration Committee.
formal.ex_us: Any amendment to the compensation package must be [[approved]] by the Compensation Committee.

everyday.ex: Legal still has [[to sign off on]] the non-compete before we send the contract out.

informal.ex: Has the CFO [[OK'd]] the package yet?

note_fr: « To validate » est un calque dans ce sens : dites « to approve », « to sign off on » ou « to clear ». UK : aussi « to sign something off » sans « on ». Ne confondez pas avec « to sign off » seul (terminer un message, ou UK : être mis en arrêt maladie par un médecin - « he's been signed off »).

def: To write the first letters of your name on a page or next to a change to show that you have seen and accepted it.

formal.ex: Each page of this contract shall be [[initialled]] by both parties.
formal.ex_us: Each page of this contract shall be [[initialed]] by both parties.

everyday.ex: Just [[put your initials]] at the bottom of each page and sign the last one.

note_fr: Orthographe : UK « initialled », US « initialed ». « To paraph » n'existe pas. La mention manuscrite « lu et approuvé » n'a pas d'équivalent : inutile de la traduire dans un contrat de droit anglais ou américain.

def: One of several identical original copies of a contract, each signed by one or more of the parties.

formal.ex: This agreement may [[be executed in counterparts]], each of which shall be deemed an original.

everyday.ex: Keep one [[signed copy]] for yourself and send the other back to HR.

note_fr: « Exemplaire » ne se traduit pas par « exemplary » (exemplaire au sens moral) ni par « example ». « En double exemplaire » : « in duplicate » ou « in two original copies ». Autre sens courant : « my counterpart in London » = mon homologue.

fr: date d'effet / date de prise d'effet
def: The date from which a contract or a change to it starts to apply.

formal.ex: This agreement shall commence on the [[Effective Date]] and continue until terminated in accordance with clause 15.

everyday.ex: Her new title applies [[as of]] 1 March.
everyday.ex_us: Her new title applies [[as of]] March 1.

note_fr: « Effective » ne veut pas dire « effectif » au sens de « réel » (« actual ») ni au sens de « effectifs » (« headcount », « workforce ») : il signifie « qui prend effet » ou « efficace ». Dates : UK « 1 March », US « March 1 ». « Actually » = en fait, « currently » = actuellement.
